Rajesh Sharma And Anr vs C.Satyam And Anr on 19 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2010 Of 2011
Judgment :

entities.text: Rajesh Sharma And Anr vs C.Satyam And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the judgment and award of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge, Nizamabad in O.P.No.648 of 2006, dated 22.04.2008 whereunder the learned Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Nizamabad awarded a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- as compensation for the death of their son in a road accident, the petitioners in the said petition have filed the present appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act and sought for enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge, Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. As could be seen from the impugned order in the present appeal, the appellants have filed the petition under Section 166 (1) (c) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 and Rule 455 of Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 and claimed compensation for the death of their son.

As per the petition, it was the case of appellants that on 23.04.2006 while the deceased was proceeding on cycle from R.P.Road to his house and when he reached Food World at Bhagath Singh Chowrastha, Nizamabad,
at about 09:00 A.M. the driver of a bus bearing No.AP-25-V-191 drove the bus in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the boy, due to which he fell down and right side rear wheel of the bus ran over him.

Though he was shifted to Government Hospital, Nizamabad, he succumbed to the injuries on the same day at 09:20 A.M.
3.

The appellants have filed the above said petition against the owner of the bus and Insurance Company from which the owner obtained policy for the bus and sought for compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
4.
Both the respondents have contested the petition.
However, the owner of the bus has claimed that in view of the policy obtained from the 2nd respondent he need not pay the compensation and sought for dismissal of the petition.
Whereas, the insurance company i.e., respondent No.2 also disputed the claim of the appellants on the ground that the driver of the vehicle had no valid license.
The bus was not in a road worthy condition and also claimed that the petition without impleading the driver of the bus is not maintainable, as such prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5 The Tribunal has framed the following (3) issues for enquiry :
1. Whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of bus bearing No.AP-25-V-191 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from which of the respondent?
3. To what relief?

entities.text: Rajesh Sharma And Anr vs C.Satyam And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. The 1st appellant herein was examined as PW1 and one Gopu Chandra Shekar has been examined as PW2.
The appellants have marked Exs.A1 to A6.
The respondents did not adduce any oral evidence, but marked the copy of Insurance Policy as Ex.B1 and the Transfer Certificate of the deceased as Ex.B2.

The Tribunal though accepted the contentions of the appellants with regard to the involvement of the bus and their right to have compensation for the untimely death of their son awarded a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- by placing reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court between New India Assurance Company vs Satender and others1.
7.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company vs Satender and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants have filed the present appeal claiming that the Tribunal failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances in a proper and perspective manner, only a meager amount of Rs.1,80,000/- was awarded without considering the income of the deceased which he used to contribute to the family.
They have also claimed that the Tribunal did not consider the age of the deceased while awarding compensation.

Therefore, according to the appellants, the Tribunal ought to have considered the age, income and future prospects for awarding compensation and also they are entitled to interest @ 9% per annum instead of 7.5% per annum as awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Heard both parties.
9. Now the point for consideration is :
Whether the Tribunal failed to consider the contentions of the appellants in proper way, thereby awarded 1 2007 (1) ALT 26 (SC) insufficient amount as compensation?
If so, whether the appellants are entitled to enhanced amount?

10. POINT:
Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that in view of the accident, the appellants lost their only son in a road accident at his tender age.
But, the Court below awarded a meager amount of Rs.1,80,000/- in spite of the fact that the appellants have filed petition for a nominal amount of Rs.4,00,000/-.

While relying on a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court between Rajendra Singh & another vs National Insurance Company Limited & others2 and in another judgment between Kishan Gopal and others vs Lala and others3, the counsel has submitted that in the case of death of a minor, earlier as per the schedule-II of M.V.Act, the notional income of the deceased was Rs.15,000/-.

entities.text: Rajendra Singh & another vs National Insurance Company Limited & others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and others vs Lala and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, in view of the later judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the notional income shall be treated as Rs.30,000/- per annum.
2 2020 ACJ 2211 3 (2014) 1 SCC 244 Therefore, the appellants are entitled to enhanced compensation.
11. There is no serious dispute about the death of deceased in the road accident.

Even though nominal objections were raised by respondent Nos.1 and 2 about the manner of accident, the oral evidence of PWs 1 and 2 coupled with the documents including charge sheet filed against the driver of the vehicle proved the accident was a result of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the van.
Therefore, the appellants are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their son.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2 respondent has filed the copy of policy by which it is very clear that as on the date of the accident,
the 1st respondent owner of the bus insured the bus with the 2nd respondent under a valid policy.
Similarly, there is no serious dispute about the validity of the driving license of the driver of the bus.
Therefore, the appellants are entitled to receive compensation from both the respondents.

12. As already stated in the previous paragraphs, the Court below having accepted the contention of the appellants while placing reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court referred supra,
granted a sum of Rs.1,80,000/-.

13. In a judgment between Kishan Gopal and Anr. vs Lala & Ors. the Hon'ble Apex Court made an observation that in case of death of a 10 years boy who was assisting their parents in their agricultural operations, it is just and reasonable to take his notional income as Rs.30,000/- per annum.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and Anr. vs Lala & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For this proposition, the principles in Lata Wadhwa and Ors. vs State of Bihar & Ors4 was relied upon.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa and Ors. vs State of Bihar & Ors4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true in the schedule-II of the M.V.Act, the amount fixed for notional income in case of the children between the age group of 10 to 15 years was Rs.15,000/- per year, but it was in the year 1994.

In the other judgment relied on by the appellants in the case of Rajendra Singh & another vs National Insurance Company Limited & others, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to observe that in case of death of a minor children, the notional income applying a 50% deductions towards personal expenses with multiplier of '15' can be 4 (2001) 8 SCC 197 awarded.

entities.text: Rajendra Singh & another vs National Insurance Company Limited & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In a recent judgment between Meena Devi vs Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto & others5 in Civil Appeal No.7255 of 2022 (arising out of Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.5345 of 2019), the Hon'ble Apex Court after considering the cases between R.K. Malik & Anr vs Kiran Pal & Ors 6, Kishan Gopal referred supra, Sarala Verma and others vs Delhi Transpport Corporation and another7 and Lata Wadhwa and Ors. Vs State of Bihar & Ors referred above, was pleaded to consider the notional income of the deceased between 10 to 15 years age group as Rs.30,000/- and enhanced the compensation.
14.

entities.text: Meena Devi vs Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto & others5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: R.K. Malik & Anr vs Kiran Pal & Ors 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others vs Delhi Transpport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa and Ors. Vs State of Bihar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, even though there is no oral evidence about the income of the deceased since there is no dispute about the age of the deceased and in the light of the above stated judgments, the appellants are entitled to enhanced compensation by treating notional income of the deceased as Rs.30,000/- per annum.
The relevant multiplier would be '15' (30,000x15=4,50,000).
Therefore, 5 2022 Live Law (SC) 841 6 2009 14 SCC 1 7 2009 6 SCC 121 the appellants are entitled to an amount of Rs.4,50,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Apart from the said amount a sum of Rs.50,000/- can be awarded under conventional head in accordance with principles in judgment between General Manager, Kerala S.R.T.C vs Susamma Thomas8 in relation to death of children between 10 to 15 years.

entities.text: General Manager, Kerala S.R.T.C vs Susamma Thomas8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants are entitled to the said compensation with interest @ 9% per annum.

It is true the appellants have filed the main petition seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-
only.

However, in view of the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and other High Courts in the recent past, even though the petition was filed for lesser amount when there is material to accept the contention of the appeal, an enhanced compensation can be awarded with a direction to the appellants/claimants to pay deficit Court fee.
15. In the result, the appeal is allowed.

A total sum of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only)
together with costs of the petition/appeal and interest @ 9% from the date of the petition has been Rajesh Sharma And Anr vs C.Satyam And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71287869/
3 awarded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants are 8 1994 2 SCC 176 entitled to receive the balance amount, after deducting the payment, if any, made by the other side, subject to their payment of deficit Court fee on the enhanced compensation.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.
